item.title: status and list --ready report items as sprint-ready even when intent gate would block them
item.intent: status 'Ready for sprint' section and 'backlog list --ready' must only show items that would actually be picked by auto — items missing or with too-short intent must be excluded.
item.description: count_ready_items() and list_ready_items() check readyForSprint==true and passes==false but do not check the intent gate (intent != null, length >= 20). PICKABLE_ITEMS_FILTER — the actual picker — requires both. So 'status' shows an inflated ready count and 'backlog list --ready' shows items that auto/run would skip. After BUG-100 adds per-item warnings when items are skipped, this display gap becomes even more visible: users see an item listed as ready in status, then get a warning that it was skipped. Fix: add the intent filter to count_ready_items and list_ready_items so that ready counts and listings reflect what is actually pickable.
steps: In count_ready_items(), add .intent != null and (.intent | length) >= 20 to the jq select filter
In list_ready_items(), add the same intent filter to the jq expression
Verify: create a test item with readyForSprint=true but no intent — confirm it is absent from 'status' ready section and 'backlog list --ready' output
Verify: items with valid intent still appear in ready sections
acceptanceCriteria: An item with readyForSprint=true and no intent does not appear under 'Ready for sprint' in 'status' output
An item with readyForSprint=true and an intent shorter than 20 chars does not appear in 'backlog list --ready'
An item with readyForSprint=true and a valid intent (>=20 chars) still appears correctly
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
